The discovery of 51 Pegasi b in 1995 by Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz was indeed the first confirmed detection of an exoplanet orbiting a main-sequence star like our Sun. This was not merely a theoretical proposal but an actual discovery based on radial velocity measurements that detected the gravitational wobble of the star 51 Pegasi caused by its orbiting planet. The discovery was groundbreaking and earned Mayor and Queloz the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics. While the detection method was indirect (radial velocity rather than direct imaging), it provided definitive confirmation of the planet's existence, not just a theoretical proposal.
